observations: The mutation kill produced the strongest possible evidence of the REAL defect: the live provider error is literally 'fiscal_year is required for CN discovery' (ValueError, retryable=false) - the year-less discovery path never worked against the real cninfo adapter, exactly as the receipt's REAL-FIX scenario claims. The gap plan failed closed (provider_unavailable=True, missing=[]) instead of fabricating a gap - LT-05 semantics confirmed against the live provider.

The discovery-year hint is load-bearing at TWO levels in the CN adapter: the API client receives fiscal_year, and the adapter re-filters candidates (year != request.fiscal_year -> drop). Removing the hint kills discovery before any download, which is why the mutation fails in 3.42s with zero bytes fetched.

The hint cannot widen or narrow downloads: it lives only in _gap_plan_result (metadata-only discovery). The authorized close-gap path downloads from gap-plan candidates; the second-request zero-download invariant is enforced by the coordinator (journal exactly one downloaded_new, files_after_first == files_after_second asserted live).

The derivation is narrowly guarded: applies only when request.fiscal_year is None (explicit-year callers untouched), and an unparsable as_of_date falls back to year-less discovery (pre-fix behavior) rather than raising. The original request_id is preserved in the gap plan; the rebuilt discovery_request derives its own deterministic id (request_id is a hash of identity including fiscal_year) - no identity collisions.

The T3 tests as shipped are structurally sound: skipUnless evaluated at import (unset env -> 's' not '.', never counted as pass), temp-wiki isolation per test (setUp/tearDown TemporaryDirectory + cleanup_temporary), byte-level hash verification of the downloaded file against snapshot_sha256, and journal-count assertions rather than result-shape inferences (scenario_matrix: counts must come from events/journal, not outcomes).
